mission: HEADROOM PHASE-3 - FORENSIC ATTRIBUTION HARNESS CLEANUP (R1, harness only)

whatChanged.new: scripts/p3-conmed-pilot/forensic-grounding.ts - assembles the evidence universe exactly as verify.ts does and calls the SAME production functions (collectNumericAssertions + groundNumericAssertions). It reimplements nothing.
whatChanged.legacyHelpers: assertedAmounts() and attributionCheck() are RETAINED, marked @deprecated with the reason, and no longer decide anything. Their only remaining callers are the explicit legacy-vs-new comparisons (forensic-grounding-replay.ts, evidence-universe-audit.ts) - keeping them is what makes the correction demonstrable instead of asserted.
whatChanged.haltSemantics: cohort A's halt kept its meaning - a figure the candidate's own anchor does not own - but now reads it off `grounding.notAnchorOwned`, which sees authenticated retrieval and normalized renderings the substring test could not.

included: every retrieved source collectAdmissibleEvidence independently re-resolved and hash-checked, carrying its retrieval identity (requestKind / scopeKey / requestKey) so R2's relation test applies
context-bundle excerpts, as CONTEXT-scope text with NO retrieval identity
evidenceUniverse.howExclusionIsEnforced: not by a filter written in the harness - by calling collectAdmissibleEvidence, which is the same authentication production uses. A refused or unresolved retrieval simply never appears in `authenticated`.
evidenceUniverse.contextBundleNote: included as a channel but structurally unable to ground: under R2 evidence with no retrieval identity can never establish a relation, so a bundle excerpt can only ever contribute to an AMBIGUOUS verdict. This is how the channel is present without granting support production would refuse.

legacyViewPolicy: supportedByAnchor / violations / unsourced remain in the report for backward-readable display ONLY, derived mechanically from assertions[].status and groundedIn, carrying deprecated:true and a derivedFrom string. Nothing reads them to decide anything; a test pins that they are disjoint and jointly complete over the asserted set.
